Republic Of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http dilg.gov.ph 13 SEP 2019 OPINION NO. MR. PAISAL O. ABUTAZIL, CESO 111 Regional Director, DILG Region IX Dear RD Abutazil: This has reference to your letter dated 01 February 2019 requesting for the Department's opinion on the issue of whether or not People's Law Enforcement Board (PLEB) members appointed by the Local Peace and Order Council (LPOC) are ipso facto resigned from their positions upon filing of Certificate of Candidacy (COC). The law is categorical that those holding public appointive office shall be considered ipso facto resigned from the filing of the COC. We find Section 66 of Batas Pambansa Blg. 881, otherwise known as the Omnibus Election Code of the Philippines, Section 24 (a) of the Commission on Elections No. 10420 promulgated on 07 September 2018, entitled "Guidelines on the Filing of Certificates of Candidacy and Nomination of Official Candidates of Registered Political Parties in Connection with the May IO, 2010 National and Local Elections," and Section 43 of Republic Act No. 6975, otherwise known as the Department of the Interior and Local Government Act of 1990, applicable to the determination of the submitted issue. Respectively, they state: "Sec. 66. Candidates holding appointive office or positions. - Any person holding a public appointive omce or position, including active members of the Armed Forces of the Philippines, and officers and employees in government-owned or controlled corporations, shall be considered ipso facto resigned from his offce upon the filing of his certificate ofcandidacy. " 'SEC. 24. Effects of Filing Certificates ofCandidacy. - a) Any person holding a public appointive office or position, including active members of the Armed Forces of the Philippines, and other officers and employees in government-owned or controlled corporations, shall be considered ipso facto

resigned from the omce and must vacate the same at the start of the day of the fling of COC. xxx" Section 43. People's Law Enforcement Board (PLEB). — (a) Creation and Functions. — Within thirty (30) days from the issuance of the implementing rules and regulations by the Commission, there shall be created by the sangguniangpanlungsod/bayan in every city and municipality such number of People 's Law Enforcement Boards (PLEBs) as may be necessary: Provided, That there shall be at least one (I) PLEB for every municipality and for each of the legislative districts in a city. The PLEB shall have jurisdiction to hear and decide citizen 's complaints or cases filed before it against erring officers and members of the PNP. There shall be at least one (1) PLEB for every five hundred (500) city or municipal police personnel. (b) Composition and Term of Office. — Th e PLEB shall be composed of the following: (1) xxx,• (2) xxx; (3) Three (3) other mem bers who shall be chosen by the peace and order council from among the respected members of the community known for their probity and integrity, one (1) of whom must be a member of the Bar or, in the absence thereof, a college graduate, or the principal of the central elementary school in the locality. (Emphasis supplied). The legal issue to resolve now is whether or not the membership in the PLEB constitutes public office. The Supreme Court defines public office, as follows: A public office is the right, authority and duty, created and conferred by law, by which, for a given period, either fixed by law or enduring at the pleasure of the creating power, an individual is invested with some portion of the sovereign functions of the government, to be exercised by him for the benefit ofthepubffc. The individual so invested is a public officer. The characteristics ofa public office, according to Mechem, include the delegation of sovereign functions, its creation bylaw and

not by contract, an oath, salary, continuing of the position, scope of duties, and the designation of the position as an office. Mechern describes the delegation to the individual of the sovereign functions of government as [t]he most important characteristic in determining whether a position is a public office or not. The most important characteristic which distinguishes an office from an employment or contract is that the creation and conferring ofan office involves a delegation to the individual ofsome of the sovereign functions of government to be exercised by him for the benefit of the public; - that some portion of the sovereignty of the country, either legislative, executive, orjudicial, attaches, for the time being, to be exercised for the public benefit. Unless the powers conferred are of this nature, the individual is not a public officer.l Further, Department of Justice Legal Opinion No. 175 series of 1991 opines in part, quote: "We find all the elements constituting a public office present in the case of membership in the PLEB, namely: (1) It is a right, authority or duty created by law (RA 6975 authorizing city/municipal sanggunians to create the PLEB; (2) such authority extends for a given period of two (2) years; and (3) the individual is vested with someportion of the sovereign powers of the government to be exercised by him for the benefit of the public, which is the jurisdiction to hear and decide citizens complaint against offices and members of the Philippine National Police. Thus, the position of a member of the PLEB is an office in a government subdivision, which may be a city or municipality, falling within the ambit of Section 7, Article IX-B of the Constitution quoted above. " In view of the foregoing, we are of the view that the members of PLEB designated by the LPOC through a Resolution, people holding appointive public office or position, shall be considered ipso facto resigned from the office and must vacate the same at the start of the day of the filing of COC. 1 Isamel G. Khan, Jr. et. Al. vs. Office of the Ombudsman, et. al. G.R. No. 125296, July 20, 2006

Nevertheless, we defer to the legal opinion of the Commission on Elections on this matter considering that it is the government agency with the mandate and, thus, the authority to rule on the same. Very truly yours, By the authority of the Secretary: MARIVEL . SACENDONCILLO, CESO 111 Undersecretary LLLS/42w
